tossups.text: Allan G. Johnson analogized this system's branching components to a tree in a book subtitled for unraveling its legacy. A 1984 Donna Haraway essay claims that the Akeley African Hall in the Museum of Natural History is an exemplar of this system's "Teddy Bear" form. A social "dividend" named for this system that benefits even "marginal" and "complacent" persons was described by Raewyn Connell in the context of a "hegemonic" identity that reinforces it. In a book on Biblical interpretation, Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza coined a term with the prefix "kyr-" for the intersectional extension of this system. bell hooks prepended "imperialist-white-supremacist-capitalist" to the name of this system, which is maintained by a "politics" that titles the magnum opus of Kate Millet. For 10 points, a feminist slogan advocates "smashing" what system of societal domination by men?
acceptableAnswers: accept anything about smashing the patriarchy
prompt on descriptive answers about male domination of society
prompt on masculinity with “what system does that reinforce?”

tossups.text: This law was strengthened by the passing of the Hatch Act, which provided funds for "experimental stations." The original bill was vetoed by Buchanan, but passed by Lincoln five years later. Its creator, a Vermont Republican, wanted each state to be given thirty thousand acres to be sold off as a permanent endowment for the teaching of "useful knowledge." For 10 points, identify this 1862 law that spurred the creation of schools dedicated to the study of "agricultural and mechanic arts."

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for esophagus and swallowing. It plays a key role in the digestive system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this esophagus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The esophagus is a key component of the Digestive system, involved in esophagus and swallowing.

tossups.text: The "Great Compression" had low levels of this condition. Emmanuel Saez and Gabriel Zucman are Berkeley economists who primarily study this condition. This condition arises when returns on capital exceed the rate of growth, or "r is greater than g," according to Capital in the Twenty-First Century by Thomas Piketty. The Lorenz curve graphs the extent of this condition, which is quantified in the Gini ("JI-nee") coefficient. Progressive taxation aims to reduce this condition. The Occupy protests centered around high levels of this condition summarized in the phrase, "We are the 99%." For 10 points, name this economic condition of uneven distribution of resources.

The Self-portrait, found in Florence, is atypical of this artist's work, which is more accurately characterized by canvases like Plowing in the Nivernais and the collections at a namesake museum in Fontainebleau. Late in life this artist traveled to Scotland to paint Highland scenes, much like her friend and chief rival Edwin Landseer. Studies for her most famous work, an enormous 1853 canvas, were made while she was disguised as a man at its namesake location. The first woman admitted to the French Legion of Honor, FTP, identify this painter of animal scenes, a native of Bordeaux who produced The Horse Fair.

In one work, David Harvey argues that this concept "annihilates space to ensure its own reproduction". A work whose title ends with this concept defines it using analysis of Benjamin Franklin's "philosophy of avarice". That work explains the development of this concept on the rise of Calvinism and analyses this concept's "spirit". In one work, Karl Marx claims that this economic system will eventually fail due to a decline in profits. Max Weber defined the "spirit" of this concept. For 10 points, what is this economic system often contrasted with socialism?

The "Gang of 14" reached an agreement to end several of these events and to prohibit their use except under "extraordinary circumstances." Mitch McConnell was the first person in history to invoke this procedure against himself during a debate on the debt ceiling crisis. In 2013, the deployment of the "nuclear option" prevented these events from happening during the confirmation of non-Supreme Court appointed officials. Rand Paul used this tactic to delay the appointment of John Brennan as Director of the CIA. For 10 points, name this legislative procedure that can be defeated when cloture is reached.
acceptableAnswers: “talking a bill to death” from British players

tossups.text: Archaeologist Betty Meggers's book on this region argued that it was never densely populated. Since the 1980s, the 364 highway has increased population density in this region despite empate ("em-PA-chih") protests by the "Gandhi" of this region, who was assassinated in 1988. A president serving in the 1950s sought to exploit the cassiterite deposits of this "unproductive and empty" region; more recently, one government has lifted the ban on correntão, a practice where two tractors are chained together to "improve" land in this region. This region was subject to the "March to the West" in the 1930s by dictator Getúlio Vargas and has more recently been clear cut for soy fields under presidents like Michel Temer ("mee-SHELL TAY-mair") and Jair Bolsonaro ("ja-EER boh-soh-NAH-roo"). For 10 points, name this Brazilian rainforest.
acceptableAnswers: accept Brazilian rainforest before the end
prompt on Western Brazil before the end

tossups.text: The potentiometric ("poh-ten-shee-oh-meh-trik") surface describes how high some types of these structures would rise if not for the presence of confining beds. A slug test measures these structures'hydraulic heads to determine their storativity. Extracting beyond the equilibrium yield of one of these structures, known as overdrafting, can result in land subsidence and saltwater intrusion. Examples of these structures include the Great Artesian Basin and the Ogallala. For 10 points, wells often access what water-containing permeable rock layers?

Programs that track this phenomenon include CompStat, which has been criticized for data manipulation and lack of impact. John Donohue and Steven Levitt claimed that this phenomenon was reduced following Roe v. Wade and popularized that claim in Freakonomics. Social pressures lead to this phenomenon according to Robert K. Merton's strain theory, while visible signs of this phenomenon encourage more of it according to the broken windows theory. The white-collar type of this behavior includes racketeering and embezzlement. For 10 points, name this behavior in which people break the law.

Philippe Pétremant folds these things to create portraits. A "security thread" is found in some of these things, which can be marked with iodine-based ink to determine their authenticity. A texture is found on part of Andrew Jackson's body, which is depicted on one of these things. "Benjamins" are a slang term for a large denomination of, for 10 points, what pieces of paper that can be exchanged for goods or services?

This composer of the oratorio The Seasons also wrote a melody on which the German anthem was based, God save Franz the Emperor. His symphonies numbers 6, 7, and 8 are titled Morning, Noon, and Evening respectively, and he also wrote a series of six "Paris Symphonies." His Farewell Symphony was composed when he took leave of Prince Esterhazy, but he is perhaps better known for another oratorio that depicts the birth of the world as described in the Book of Genesis. The composer of the Miracle, Military, Surprise, and Clock symphonies, for 10 points, identify this Austrian composer of the oratorio The Creation and the "London Symphonies."

Jan Tinbergen applied Newton's law of universal gravitation to predict the magnitude of this phenomenon. Leontief's paradox refutes the Hecksher-Ohlin model of this phenomenon in labor and capital intensive countries. Gains from this phenomenon come from lower opportunity costs of production according to David Ricardo's theory of comparative advantage. In the 17th century, restrictions on this action in European colonies promoted the economic policy of mercantilism, which sought to maximize exports and minimize imports. In recent years, the "free" variety of this practice has been promoted by agreements like NAFTA. For 10 points, name this exchange of goods and services between countries.

One of these conflicts began while an army was deployed to decide the "eastern question" once and for all, and was exacerbated by the governor Rufus. Josephus was a prominent historian of these conflicts, and one of these conflicts ended in a mass suicide after the invaders built a causeway to capture the fortress of Masada. The Sicarii and Zealots agitated to begin one of these conflicts, and Simon bar Kokhba led one of these conflicts in a certain Middle Eastern Roman province. For 10 points, describe these military insurrections that occurred in the province of Judea and tended to cause the destruction of Jerusalem.

This property can be measured using a Zahn cup, and for special cases, shear stress can be calculated as the product of shear strain and this property. Measuring this is the goal of the pitch drop experiment, and one unit this quantity is measured in is poise. Stokes' law gives drag force for a spherical object as six pi times radius times velocity times this property, and the Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial forces to forces caused by this. This property has a constant value for Newtonian fluids, and it exists in kinematic and dynamic forms. For 10 points, name this term for a fluid's resistance to flow.

The domes El Solo and El Fraile are found on this peak. The Barranca Blanca is a canyon on its northwest slope. Portuzuelo Negro (por-tu-SWAY-lo NE-gro) is a source of desperately needed water during the ascent of this peak. A modified vehicle race to the top of this peak uses the highest four-wheel drive road in the world and was nearly completed in 2007. That road ends at Refugio Tejos (re-FOO-hi-yo TE-hos), although most climbers stop at the canyon of the Cazadero de Quemadito (ca-sa-DE-ro de ke-ma-DEE-to), following which its first field of penitentes is encountered at Agua de las Vicuñas. Volcán El Muerto is a side vent of this peak. A dispute considering the height of nearby Monte Pissis involves a local record held by this mountain, and a better-known record, in the absence of fumarolic activity, would be held by Llullaillaco (yu-ya-YA-ko). For 10 points, name this tallest active volcano in the world, the highest point in Chile, named for an anthropomorphic feature that forms at the intersection of its glacial lakes and its halite deposits.

This country was the setting for Guillermo Cabrera Infante's experimental novel Tres Tristes Tigres, which features a section titled "Some Revelations" which comprises blank pages. Reinaldo Arenas described government persecution based on his open homosexuality in this country in his autobiography Before Night Falls. The Latin American Boom author of the novel The Kingdom of This World, Alejo Carpentier, lived his adult life in this country. A poem from the collection Versos Sencillos has been adopted as this country's unofficial national song. For 10 points, "Guantanamera" by Jose Marti describes a woman from what Caribbean country's city of Guantanamo?

The title character serves in Reverend Soulis's manse in this author's "Thrawn Janet," from The Merry Men. Keawe sells a container with an inexhaustible supply of whiskey in his The Bottle Imp. He wrote about a protagonist who marries James More's daughter after Alan Breck Stewart is falsely convicted of the Appin murder, in Catriona. He wrote of James Durie joining the Jacobite Uprising, and of Captain Hoseason purchasing David Balfour. In another novel of his, Jim Hawkins meets Long John Silver. For 10 points, who wrote The Master of Ballantrae, Kidnapped, and Treasure Island?

Lord Paul Rziczan read a letter aloud at this event before whipping out his pistols and firing a warning shot. Another participant in this event yelled "Jesus" and "Mary" repeatedly while another had his fingers smashed first. Three sandstones mark the place of this event during which Filip Fabricius earned the nickname "von Hohenfall." The causes of this event stemmed from a document issued by Rudolf II that was later ignored by Ferdinand II. That document, the Letter of Majesty, was the subject of the trial of William Slavata and Jaroslav Marinic who were involved in this event, which took place at Hradcany Castle. Although participants in this event later claimed to be saved by divine intervention, their enemies claimed they instead fell in horse manure. For 10 points, name this event which sparked the Thirty Years' War during which three men were thrown from a window in Bohemia.
acceptableAnswers: but do not accept “First Defenestration of Prague”
